practices.practice: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable at runtime and fail early if it is missing; do not embed credentials in source files.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code credentials or write the URI into logs or committed files.

practices.practice: Create a single MongoClient (process-wide singleton) and reuse it across the app instead of opening a new client per request; configure and tune connection-pool parameters to suit serverless vs long-running workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single MongoClient/MongoClient-like connection object across the app (create once at process start and share), and configure a connection pool (e.g. maxPoolSize) rather than opening a new connection per request.

practices.practice: Require TLS for all connections (connection strings include tls=true) and restrict network access with firewall rules or Private Endpoints so only authorized app runtimes can reach the cluster.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for all connections (connection string must include tls/ssl=true or use the mongodb+srv scheme), and restrict network access via firewall/VNet rules so only the app runtime IPs can reach the cluster.

practices.practice: Avoid committing raw credentials to source; provide a .env.example with a placeholder connection string and instruct users to set the real value via environment variables or a secrets manager.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing raw secret keys in code or repository examples; include a .env.example with placeholder DOCUMENTDB_URI and document how to set real values in environment variables or a secrets manager.

practices.practice: Give application credentials least privilege: create a database-scoped user for the sample app instead of using an admin key or cluster-wide credentials.
practices.prior_belief: Keep database-level credentials with least privilege for the sample: create a user scoped to the sample_fintech_04 database and avoid using a full-admin key in the sample's configuration.

practices.practice: Record the embedding vector, embedding model name and the vector dimensionality alongside the text so index creation and later queries can verify compatibility.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the vector dimensionality and ensure embedding model choice matches provisioned vector index dims to avoid incompatible insert/query errors (document the model name and dims=384 in README and .env.example).

practices.practice: When provisioning a vector index, set the index type and dimensions to match your embedding model (choose diskANN for large production sets, HNSW for smaller sets, IVF for tiny sets) and set similarity (e.g., COS for cosine) in the index definition.
practices.prior_belief: Provision a vector-capable collection/index with parameters that match the embedding dimension: set vector index dims=384 (embedding model all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and choose the cluster-supported index type (e.g., vector-diskann or HNSW/IVF) and cosine similarity (metric=COS) when creating the index.

practices.practice: Also create conventional single-field or compound indexes on frequently filtered fields (e.g., transcript_id, source, chunk_id, start_time) so filter-by-transcript and time-range queries are efficient.
practices.prior_belief: Also create conventional indexes on fields used for filtering or grouping (e.g., transcript_id, chunk_id, start_timestamp) to make filter-by-transcript or time-range queries efficient.

practices.practice: Store embeddings in a documented field together with metadata and the embedding dimensions and model name (the DB may accept arrays or specialized formats such as quantized/fp16; document what you use so index creation matches the stored shape).
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as an array of floats of length 384 (or the database-specific binary vector format expected by the engine) and document the exact vector shape and field name used so index creation and queries match.

practices.practice: Run nearest-neighbor queries using the cluster's vector search API (cosmosSearch / $search) with a topK parameter and tune search parameters (lSearch / k / score thresholds); combine with projections to return only needed fields to reduce bandwidth.
practices.prior_belief: Implement NN search using the cluster's vector search API/operator and restrict returned fields via projection (text, timestamps, transcript_id, score) to reduce bandwidth; ensure the vector search call includes 'topK' and an appropriate score threshold.

practices.practice: Apply metadata-based pre-filtering (for example by transcript/source or date range or partition key) as part of or before vector search to reduce fan-out and improve precision and RU/IO costs.
practices.prior_belief: Apply metadata-based pre-filtering (e.g., transcript_id or date range) before or as part of vector search to reduce candidate set and improve precision for domain-specific queries.

practices.practice: When returning results, project only the needed fields and limit/paginate results (limit topK to a reasonable number like 10–50) so post-processing and LLM context assembly stays within memory and token budgets.
practices.prior_belief: Use projection and pagination: when scanning results fetch only needed fields and paginate/limit responses (e.g., limit topK to 10-50) so post-processing and LLM context assembly stays within memory and token limits.

practices.practice: Make ingestion idempotent: deduplicate documents using a deterministic key (e.g., transcript + chunk id checksum) or upsert semantics so re-running ingestion doesn't create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Before inserting chunks, deduplicate by a deterministic key (e.g., transcript_id + chunk_id + checksum) or use upsert semantics so re-running ingestion is idempotent and does not create duplicate embeddings/index entries.

practices.practice: Implement exponential backoff and retries for transient network errors and throttling (429), and make writes idempotent (upsert) so retries don't create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Use exponential backoff and retry for transient network errors and rate limits when calling the database or embedding model; make writes idempotent or use upserts so retries don't duplicate data.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings (e.g., unit-length) when using cosine similarity and store the embedding model name and dimensions with each document so queries and index parameters can be validated.
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as an array of floats of length 384 (or the database-specific binary vector format expected by the engine) and document the exact vector shape and field name used so index creation and queries match.

practices.practice: Store text chunks and their embedding together in the same document (text, timestamps, source, embedding, embedding_model, embedding_dims, inserted_at) to avoid extra lookups during retrieval and to enable direct citation.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single collection (or logically separate collections) that stores the text chunk and its embedding in the same document so nearest-neighbor retrieval returns text and metadata without an extra lookup.

practices.practice: Record provenance metadata per chunk (source filename, chunk id, start/end timestamps, ingestion time, embedding model) so answers can cite exact transcripts and timestamps.
practices.prior_belief: Record provenance metadata per chunk (source filename, original page/line offsets, timestamp, ingestion time, embedding model used) and include those fields in query results to allow verifiable citations in LLM responses.

practices.practice: Monitor index and query performance (enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation) and use the MCP inspection tools to validate created indexes and query plans.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor index and query performance (index build times, disk usage, query latencies, topK recall) and set alerts when vector index memory/disk pressure or query latencies exceed thresholds; use the MCP server tools to inspect created indexes and query plans.

practices.practice: Tune vector-index build/search parameters appropriate to the chosen engine (e.g., lBuild/lSearch/maxDegree for DiskANN, HNSW/IVF parameters or product-quantization settings) to trade off recall vs latency and memory.
practices.prior_belief: When creating the vector index, pick and tune index-specific parameters (e.g., efConstruction, efSearch, M for HNSW or IVF/centroids settings) appropriate to DiskANN/HNSW/IVF index type and expected query throughput/recall tradeoffs.

practices.practice: Enable provider-managed backups and understand the service's automatic backup retention (point-in-time recovery); treat heavy ingest/index operations with care and ensure you have a restore plan.
practices.prior_belief: Back up the database or enable provider-managed backups before bulk ingest or index builds; large vector indexes and bulk loads can be expensive to roll back.

practices.practice: When running ingestion, batch inserts (use bulk/insertMany or provider bulk APIs) to improve throughput and failure handling rather than issuing single-document writes one at a time.

practices.practice: Use application-side cosine calculation only as a fallback; prefer built-in vector search APIs for scale and performance when a vector index is available on the cluster.
Use the DocumentDB MCP server tools (or provider management UI) to inspect index definitions, validate document counts, and verify what the ingestion created as part of automation verification.
practices.prior_belief: When verifying index creation and document inserts in automation, use the cluster's management/inspection tools (the DocumentDB MCP server helpers or equivalent) to fetch index definitions and validate document counts; treat any failure in those checks as a blocking issue for verification.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB storage uses premium SSD options and IOPS/bandwidth is gated by compute tier (not RU model); size compute for throughput requirements rather than sizing disk for IOPS.
practices.prior_belief: For performance and cost reasons, batch inserts of document+embedding (e.g., 100–1000 docs per bulk insert) rather than inserting one document at a time during ingestion, and monitor RU/throughput or equivalent credits during bulk loads.

practices.practice: Use context-engineering rules to assemble retrieved passages to fit the LLM token budget: rank by vector score, concatenate until budget minus answer buffer is reached, and favor distinct timestamps to improve coverage.

I used installed skills (documentdb-*) as authoritative public guidance where available and Microsoft Learn quickstarts/docs for connection, backup and insert behavior. The workspace app implements many of the confirmed practices (env var, singleton client, storing embedding+metadata, unique chunk_id index, insert_many bulk insert).
